ANSWER / HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded):
The variable is RACE (race/ethnicity). The association of being Black or Hispanic (relative to White) with BA degree completion is strong and significant in the univariate model but shrinks by roughly 5–6× and becomes statistically non-significant once SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite + percentile-in-class) are added — i.e., the racial/ethnic gap in BA completion is largely explained by socioeconomic status and academic preparation. In this subset the single cleanest dummy match is the BLACK (vs. White) category, with Hispanic showing the same direction and also losing significance.

WHY RACE IS THE ANSWER:
- Only the race dummies both (a) are significant in Model A and (b) become non-significant in Model B (Black p .000→.54; Hispanic p .003→.26) with a several-fold shrinkage.
- Family size stays highly significant (ratio 1.00); sex was non-significant in both models (ratio 0.91); SES/ability/percentile are the controls and remain significant. So no other social-background variable fits.
- OLS LPM cross-check agrees: Black LPM -0.0180 (p<.001) → +0.0050 (p=0.24); Hispanic -0.0148 (p=0.003) → -0.0051 (p=0.30).

VIFs (full adjusted model): black 1.35, hisp 1.24, male 1.04, famsize 1.15, ses 1.39, ability 2.73, percentile 2.08 — all < 3, so no serious multicollinearity; the race effect is genuinely explained away, not a collinearity artifact.

COEFFICIENT-TYPE NOTE (the 0.5024/0.0923): I could not reproduce these literal values in this 8,773-row subset under any form (raw log-odds, OR, standardized OLS or logit). Their ratio (~5.4×) and the requirement of 'becomes insignificant' match RACE best — specifically the Black (vs. White) contrast, whose magnitude drops ~6× (log-odds) and whose standardized logit β drops from -0.375 to +0.058. The exact 0.5024/0.0923 almost certainly come from the original full-NLS sample and a specific race coding/scaling; the direction, ~5× shrinkage, and loss of significance are reproduced here.

LIMITATIONS:
- Curriculum (the third 'academic characteristic' in the metadata) is absent from the CSV, so academic characteristics = ASVAB composite + percentile-in-class only.
- Rare outcome (2.69%): SEs/significance are sensitive; OLS LPM cross-check included and agrees.
- The literal 0.5024/0.0923 are not reproduced in this subset; the match is by pattern (variable, direction, ~5× shrinkage, loss of significance), not exact value.
